history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. The Mahant Ghasidas Memorial Museum is an archaeological museum on Raj Bhawan Road (Civil Lines, near Ghadi Chowk) in Raipur — one of the oldest museums of Chhattisgarh and among the first ten museums of India. Built in 1875 by Mahant Raja Ghasi Das of Rajnandgaon (initially run by the municipality and zilla parishad); renovated in 1953 by Rani Jyoti Devi and her son Digvijay Das (Rs 1 lakh), with the new building inaugurated by President Rajendra Prasad. Five galleries across three floors cover archaeology, natural history, tribal culture, inscriptions, coins, weapons and paintings; the campus was later developed as Sanskriti Bhawan. It is also known as 'Ajaib Bangla'. Opening-hours conflict across sources: 10:30 AM–4:30 PM closed Tuesday (travelsetu, wanderboat) vs 10 AM–5 PM closed Monday (tripxl) — verify locally. Entry: INR 10 adult / INR 5 child per travelsetu.
